content: A polymer blend, also referred to as a polymer alloy or polymer mixture, is a type of material that is conceptually similar to metal alloys. In this material, two or more polymers are combined to form a new substance with distinct physical properties that differ from those of the individual components. Polymer blends are generally categorized into three main types: miscible blends, partially miscible blends, and immiscible blends. Among these, immiscible blends are the most commonly encountered group. Reference: Gert R. Strobl (1996). The Physics of Polymers: Concepts for Understanding Their Structures and Behavior. Springer-Verlag.
